text: Two monks came to a river, swollen with rain.
A young woman stood on the bank. She could not cross.
The monks had sworn never to touch a woman.
But the old monk lifted her onto his back, and waded in.
On the far side, he set her down. She bowed, and was gone.
The monks walked on. For hours, the young one said nothing.
But his anger grew heavier with every step.
At nightfall, he burst out: "How could you carry that woman?"
The old monk smiled. "I put her down at the river."
Put down what you carry. The river is already behind you.
